heard: A single teaspoon of a neutron star weighs one billion tons. That is roughly 900 times the weight of the Great Pyramid of Giza. Neutron stars are the collapsed cores of supergiant stars that died in a supernova. In 1967, graduate student Jocelyn Bell-Burnell detected a radio pulse so rhythmic she nicknamed it Little Green Men. These remnants pack the mass of a sun into a city-sized sphere, only 12 miles wide. The star's gravity is so intense that the escape velocity exceeds half the speed of light. In 2017, the LIGO Observatory detected two of these giants colliding to forge the world's gold and platinum. These cosmic impacts created the heavy metals found in our jewelry today, but their origin remains unimaginably dense.
